instruction:
Use NOAA National Ocean Service Ocean Facts to answer a four-part ocean-science brief. Locate Why is the ocean salty?, Why is the ocean blue?, How deep is the ocean?, and What is a hydrothermal vent?. Explain the two main sources of ocean salt and identify the two most prevalent dissolved ions and their combined share as stated on the page. Explain the stated reason for blue ocean water and one reason it can appear another color. Record the stated average ocean depth, deepest location and its approximate depth, preserving units. Connect the hydrothermal-vent account to the salt explanation: describe how vent water is heated and why it can remain liquid at the stated high temperature. Use four separate article citations and report the page values observed during the run. Use the written articles on NOAA pages for the explanation.

Stopping condition: Stop when all four parts are answered with the requested units, causal connection and citations to the four NOAA Ocean Facts articles.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Evaluate if the agent identified the two main sources of ocean salt and the two most prevalent dissolved ions along with their combined share, as stated on the NOAA page during the run. Full credit if all requested elements are accurately reported, OR if the agent attempts to access the page and clearly reports that the site is down or the specific information is no longer present. Partial credit if only some of the available elements are provided.

Evaluate if the agent explained the stated reason for blue ocean water and one reason it can appear another color based on the NOAA page. Full credit if both reasons are accurately reported based on current page content, OR if the agent properly attempts the search and accurately reports that the page or details are unavailable. Partial credit if only one of these explanations is provided when both are available.

items.criterion: Record 'How deep is the ocean?' statistics
items.description: Evaluate if the agent recorded the stated average ocean depth and the deepest location along with its approximate depth, preserving units. Full credit if the average depth, deepest location name, and its depth are provided with their respective units, OR if the agent reports the current values on the page if they have changed, OR if the agent reports the site/information is unavailable. Partial credit if units are missing or if only partial statistics are provided despite being available.

Evaluate if the agent described how vent water is heated, why it can remain liquid at the stated high temperature, and how the vent account connects to the explanation of ocean salt, based on the written NOAA articles. Full credit if these requested explanations and the causal connection are accurate, OR if the agent accurately reports that the page or specific details are unavailable. Partial credit if available requested explanations or the connection are missing.

Evaluate if the agent included four separate article citations (e.g., URLs) for the four NOAA Ocean Facts topics used to compile the brief. Full credit if four appropriate NOAA links are provided, including links to pages that returned errors if the site was down. Partial credit for 1-3 correct links. No credit if no sources are cited.
